name: W Sydney
positioning: A curving, futuristic tower rising over Darling Harbour, with marine-inspired rooms where no two are alike, a rooftop infinity pool and a two-storey rooftop bar
best_for: Design-minded travelers who want harbour views and a lively rooftop scene
Longer stays or families in the one- to three-bedroom Studio apartments

facts.text: Room interiors take their palette from the surrounding marine environment.
The interiors draw on the free-spirited Australian larrikin.
The indoor WET pool on Level 22 has a waratah-inspired mosaic mural.
29/30 is a two-storey rooftop bar at the hotel's crown above Darling Harbour.
One-, two- and three-bedroom Studio apartments with full gourmet kitchens are designed for longer stays.
A scenic waterfront walking trail leads from the hotel area via Pyrmont and the Barangaroo headland toward Sydney's icons.
Every guestroom and venue has harbour or city views.
Penthouse I on Level 27 channels the HMAS Onslow submarine and has a crescent-shaped bedroom and a circular bathtub overlooking the harbour.

highlights.text: W Sydney rises over Darling Harbour with the undulating lines of a futuristic exterior.
The rooftop WET Deck has a heated infinity pool with 180-degree views of Darling Harbour.
No two rooms are alike; they have floor-to-ceiling windows with views over Darling Harbour or the city.
AWAY Spa has five treatment rooms, manicure and pedicure pods, a relaxation zone, a sauna, a steam room and a beauty bar.

considerations.text: Rooms do not permit rollaway beds.
Valet parking is limited and must be pre-booked.
WhataHotel notes the trendy, party-focused atmosphere may not suit traditional luxury travelers.
